free_tier.stated: Free plan at USD 0 with '20K credits / month' plus '$1 prepaid agents / month'. The plan table converts that for you: Sonic-3.6 text to speech gets '~27' minutes a month at '2' concurrent requests, Ink-2 speech to text gets '~1h 51m' a month at '8' concurrent requests, and managed agents get 17 minutes at USD 0.06 a minute. The FAQ gives the unit: 'Sonic text-to-speech: One minute of audio generation requires 750-800 credits. 1 credit equals 1 character' and 'Ink speech-to-text: 3 credits equals 1 second of audio'.

record.interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
record.chaining: a free plan here covers the STT side of a demo better than the TTS side, because 20,000 credits at 3 credits a second is 1h51m of transcription while the same pool is only 27 minutes of speech. What breaks: any repeated synthesis, since 27 minutes a month does not accumulate and the plan is monthly rather than annual.

limits.value: 27 minutes of generated speech a month, then the pool is empty; the 2-request TTS concurrency ceiling means a batch of short clips still cannot be pushed in one afternoon without queueing, but the volume runs out first.

record.category: text-to-speech and speech-to-text API, monthly free credit pool

free_tier.stated: Free plan at USD 0 a month with 20K credits per month plus USD 1 of prepaid voice-agent usage per month. The credits are spent on text-to-speech at 1 credit per character (about 750 to 800 credits per minute of audio, which the plan table puts at about 27 minutes of Sonic-3.6 a month) or on speech-to-text at 3 credits per second of audio (about 1h 51m of Ink-2 a month); the USD 1 of agent usage is about 33 minutes at USD 0.03 a minute, before telephony and language-model usage.
free_tier.notes: models: text-to-speech sonic-3.6 (44 languages; sonic-3.5 and sonic-3 also accepted by the API) and speech-to-text Ink-2; managed voice agents. unverified: whether unused Free credits roll over, because the pricing page describes rollover only in terms of paid plans

record.interface_detail: REST (POST /tts/bytes and sibling TTS and STT routes) and WebSocket at api.cartesia.ai, versioned by a Cartesia-Version header; Python and JavaScript quickstarts
record.tooling: raw HTTP and WebSocket with an API key (sk_car_...) from the playground, or the Python and JavaScript quickstarts
record.chaining: the monthly pool covers the speech-to-text side of a demo better than the text-to-speech side, because 20K credits is about 1h 51m of Ink-2 transcription but only about 27 minutes of Sonic-3.6 speech; run it from a free CI job for small voice-over or transcription batches. Unlike a one-time credit it renews each month.

limits.value: 20K credits per month on the Free plan, shared by text-to-speech and speech-to-text, plus USD 1 per month of prepaid voice-agent usage; with overages off, new requests are blocked once the credits run out
Free plan concurrency: 2 concurrent text-to-speech requests and 8 concurrent speech-to-text requests; on Free plans a request over the limit returns 429 immediately, where paid plans queue it

record.binding_note: about 27 minutes of Sonic-3.6 speech or about 1h 51m of Ink-2 transcription per month runs out before the concurrency caps matter

identity_cost.detail: the signup form asks for a first name, last name, email address and password, or a GitHub or Google account; the pricing page names no card for the Free plan and the signup form shows none; unverified: whether a phone number, a card or a verification step is asked after the form

record.reliability_note: a Free-plan request over the concurrency limit fails with 429 instead of queuing
record.confidence_note: the credit pool, the credit costs, the converted minutes and the concurrency table are quoted from vendor pages; rollover on Free and the card requirement at signup are unverified.
